bullets.title: NVDA Q2 FY27 Beats Across the Board; FY28 Guide ~70% — Supply Constrained
bullets.body: Nvidia reported Q2 FY27 revenue of $96.2B (vs. $92.2–92.4B est), +106% YoY, +18% QoQ; data center $89B (+117% YoY) vs. $85.9B est; adj. EPS $2.22 vs. $2.09–2.10 est; adj. gross margin 75%. Q3 guide: $108B ±2% (vs. $104.2B est), adj. GM 73.5–74.5% (vs. ~75% est). CFO guided FY28 revenue growth ~70%, characterized as supply-constrained — implying actual demand runs materially higher. One analyst noted demand exceeds 70%, with company 'capacity constraining delivery.' Stock initially dipped, then rallied 5–7% as the FY28 guide landed.

bullets.title: NVDA AWS Partnership: 2M Additional GPUs; OpenAI 12GW Commitment Through 2030
bullets.body: On the earnings call, NVIDIA and AWS announced deployment of 2 million additional GPUs across AWS global infrastructure through Q2 2029, plus 100K-GPU secure clusters for U.S. government. Jensen Huang cited OpenAI's existing and planned commitments representing ~12GW of Nvidia compute through 2030. NVDA also entered MOUs with large capital providers in August to mobilize $500B+ in third-party project financing.

bullets.title: NVDA Acquires Hugging Face for ~$12.9B — AI Ecosystem Play
bullets.body: The Information reported Nvidia agreed to acquire open-source AI model repository Hugging Face for $12.9B, extending NVIDIA's control over AI model distribution and developer tooling. Multiple sources confirmed the deal across the digest window.

bullets.title: NVDA Custom NVHBM Memory: 30% More Bandwidth, 15% Lower Power vs. HBM4E
bullets.body: NVIDIA introduced NVHBM, a custom high-bandwidth memory that integrates the memory controller into the 3D HBM stack rather than on the XPU, delivering up to 30% greater memory bandwidth, 15% lower power, and freeing ~25% more compute die area versus standard HBM4E. One analyst noted NVIDIA has 'reserved a massive amount of memory' tied to this development.

bullets.title: NVDA FY28 Guide Raises Supply Chain Read-Throughs; Non-NVDA Names May Face Estimate Cuts
bullets.body: Post-earnings commentary flagged ABF substrates and PCB/CCL as the binding 2027 bottleneck — not HBM or DRAM. One analyst said '2026 substrate capacity fully booked, 12–14 month lead times.' Separately, an analyst warned shipment forecasts for non-NVIDIA players including AMD and Broadcom may need to be cut. COHR and LITE named as well-positioned; CEG and VST flagged as AI power demand beneficiaries.

bullets.title: Memory Cycle Bullish: DRAM Near 5-Year Highs, Structural Shortage Anticipated Through 2027
bullets.body: One analyst noted 1kg of South Korean DRAM now costs the equivalent of 620g of gold, up from 120g at the 2023 trough, as AI demand drives prices to multi-year highs. Separately, commentary flagged panic-hoarding by buyers anticipating 2027 structural memory shortages, with Winbond exiting DDR2 to focus on DDR4/3 and capacity discussions running through 2029–2030. Post-NVDA earnings, market consensus described as 'bullish on memory.'

bullets.title: MRVL Pre-Earnings: Optical Multi-Chip Interconnect Bridge & $3.25B Photonic Fabric Acquisition
bullets.body: Ahead of Marvell's earnings, an optics sector analyst highlighted MRVL's $3.25B acquisition of a Photonic Fabric company as core technology — extracting memory from the package and connecting via light. MRVL is also expected to announce its Optical Multi-Chip Interconnect Bridge (OMIB) technology, with the same research authors' institutional email domain changing between ECTC papers published a year apart.

bullets.title: META $18B Settlement on Youth Harm Claims; Stock Rises ~1.7%
bullets.body: Meta agreed to pay up to $18B to settle U.S. states' claims over social media harm to youth and improper child data collection. Markets viewed the outcome positively — perceived as far less damaging than a $1.4T worst-case risk — with shares rising ~1.7%. Meta will also face tougher teen safety and age-verification rules, including two-hour daily limits for U.S. teens on Facebook and Instagram.

bullets.title: Salesforce Beats Q2, Announces 'ClaudeForce' Anthropic Integration
bullets.body: Salesforce reported Q2 revenue of $11.35B (vs. $11.32B est) and adj. EPS $5.90; raised FY revenue guidance to $46.1–46.4B and guided Q3 at $11.42–11.5B. Concurrently, Salesforce and Anthropic announced ClaudeForce — Claude AI embedded in Salesforce with open beta expected September 2026.

bullets.title: Intel EMIB Packaging Confirmed TSMC Rival; 18A Yields Ahead of Targets
bullets.body: Multiple sources confirmed Intel's EMIB advanced packaging is a confirmed rival to TSMC, with strong yields and satisfied customers including Google and MediaTek. At Deutsche Bank conference, Intel management was upbeat on foundry and process node developments with 18A yields tracking ahead of internal targets.

bullets.title: Samsung/SK Hynix Shift to HBM4 8-Stack; NVIDIA Supply Chain Diversifying
bullets.body: Samsung and SK Hynix are increasing HBM4 8-stack shipment share, signaling a shift in Nvidia's HBM supply chain. Separately, NVIDIA stated memory supply will remain a bottleneck through at least the end of FY28 — compressing margins — with Q3 gross margin guided at 73.5–74.5% vs. ~75% expected.

bullets.title: SanDisk/Kioxia Plan $31B Memory Fab Expansion in Japan
bullets.body: SanDisk and Kioxia announced a combined $31B memory fab expansion in Japan. Separately, Kioxia plans to invest ¥1 trillion ($6.27B) to build a third fab in Iwate Prefecture with operations starting in 2029 and government subsidies expected.

bullets.title: NVDA Commitments Surge to $279B QoQ; $63B Accounts Receivable Flagged
bullets.body: NVIDIA disclosed supplier commitments more than doubled quarter-over-quarter from $119B to $279B, reflecting multi-year demand visibility. Credit investors raised concerns about NVIDIA's balance sheet, flagging the company as 'Central Bank of AI' with $63.1B in accounts receivable and rising leverage — a notable divergence from equity market enthusiasm.

bullets.title: BOJ's Himino: Rate Hikes Coming — Won't Wait for Full Data; FX Impacts Monitored
bullets.body: BOJ Deputy Governor Himino signaled proactive monetary tightening: policy 'will not wait until full information' is available; could 'speed up rate hikes if financial conditions remain too accommodative.' He noted consumer inflation likely above 2% in FY's latter half. Short/medium-term real borrowing costs remain below zero and JGB taper can proceed as planned.

bullets.title: Alibaba Commits $57B to AI Over 3 Years; Launches Low-Cost Qwen 3.8-Flash Model
bullets.body: Alibaba committed 380 billion yuan ($57B) to AI over three years and raised HK$80B for Qwen global expansion. Concurrently, Alibaba launched Qwen 3.8-Flash-Next, targeting global adoption through competitive performance and low inference costs.

bullets.title: Core PCE 3.3% in July — 65 Months Above Fed Target; Atlanta Fed GDPNow at +4.6%
bullets.body: Core PCE rose to 3.3% YoY in July, 65 consecutive months above the Fed's 2% target, with headline CPI at 3.4%. Meanwhile, the Atlanta Fed's GDPNow model upgraded Q3 2026 real GDP to +4.6% from +4.0%, creating a stagflation-adjacent backdrop as rate-cut expectations fade.

bullets.title: T-Glass Supply Expanding; Chinese Vendors Enter Market, Easing Bottleneck
bullets.body: Commentary from supply chain sources noted Chinese vendors entering the T-glass market aggressively, expanding supply from a near-Nittobo monopoly to 5+ suppliers — potentially relieving a key constraint for advanced packaging. TSMC had previously cited T-glass impact on CoWoS yield and reliability.

bullets.title: NVDA Earnings Reaction: Asia-Pac Chipmakers Rally; Futures +0.9% Nasdaq Pre-Market
bullets.body: Following NVDA's report, S&P 500 futures climbed 0.47% and Nasdaq futures advanced 0.9%. Asia-Pacific equities opened mostly positive led by chipmakers. One analyst noted NVDA is on track for its first positive earnings-day reaction in five quarters if gains hold through close.

bullets.title: US Army Awards $2.2B Nuclear Microreactor Contract; Power Grid Equipment Ban
bullets.body: The U.S. Army awarded up to $2.2B across five companies (Antares, BWXT, General Atomics, Radiant, Westinghouse) to build and operate nuclear microreactors at five military bases. Separately, Trump signed an executive order banning certain foreign-made (primarily Chinese) energy equipment from the U.S. power grid, with DOE given 120 days to implement rules — bullish for domestic grid equipment makers CEG and OKLO flagged as relevant.

bullets.title: MLCC Upcycle Starting: SEMCO Leads 4Q26 OEM Price Hikes
bullets.body: TrendForce reports Samsung Electro-Mechanics is leading MLCC price hikes for OEM/ODM customers starting 4Q26, with increases previously concentrated among smaller suppliers now broadening — signaling the start of an industry upcycle.
